c.tagline: West Bohemia's grand belle-époque spa town of thermal springs, colonnades and Becherovka

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered but agree a price for longer trips. Ride-hailing (Uber/Bolt) is limited outside Prague, so a phoned or ranked taxi is usually the reliable option in Karlovy Vary.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-wide emergency number and connects to English-speaking operators. Dial 155 for an ambulance and 158 for the police directly.

hood_landmark.Lázeňské centrum: Mill Colonnade Mlynska kolonada Karlovy Vary
hood_landmark.Tuhnice: Tuhnice Karlovy Vary Ohre river KV Arena

avoid.reason: Agree taxi fares or use apps to avoid overcharging, and skip poor-rate currency exchange booths along the spa colonnades.

hood_desc: The Lázeňské centrum (spa district) is the postcard heart of Karlovy Vary: belle-époque facades in pastel colors line the Teplá river, and grand colonnades shelter a dozen thermal springs. Sip warm mineral water from a porcelain spa cup, watch the Vřídlo geyser erupt, and stroll from the Mill Colonnade to the Market Colonnade.

Drahovice is a quiet, largely residential hillside neighborhood east of the center. It offers everyday Czech life, leafy streets, cheaper eats, and easy bus links back to the colonnades, making it a calm base away from the spa crowds.

Rybáře is the busy commercial district north of the river, home to shops, supermarkets, the main market area and practical services. It is where locals run errands and where you'll find more affordable dining and lodging.

Tuhnice sits west of the center along the Ohře river and hosts the KV Arena, the Becherovka distillery area and modern apartment blocks. It's a convenient, down-to-earth part of town within a short bus ride of the spa promenade.
Stará Role is a further-out residential suburb to the northwest with a village feel, parks and family homes. It's the most affordable place to stay and connects to the center by frequent city buses.
lodging: Carlsbad Plaza Medical Spa & Wellness Hotel

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink; the hot spring waters are for sipping cures only.

transit.hours: Approx. 4:30-23:00, with night lines on some routes
transit.note: Karlovy Vary has no tram or metro; the DPKV network is entirely city buses. Buy tickets from the driver or machines and validate on board. The compact spa center is best explored on foot.
transit.pay: Cash or contactless on board; tickets also via app

air: Karlovy Vary Airport (KLV), 6 km, limited scheduled flights
Most travelers use Prague Airport (PRG), ~122 km
bus: FlixBus, RegioJet and Student Agency coaches connect Prague and Prague Airport (~1h 25m-1h 30m)
Regional and international coaches from Terminal Bus Station
train: Czech Railways (CD) via Karlovy Vary dolni nadrazi and horni nadrazi to Prague, Cheb and Chomutov

transit.m: City bus No. 8 from airport to Trznice (Market) stop (~20-25 min)
Taxi from KLV to spa center (10-15 min)
Most visitors fly into Prague (PRG, ~122 km); FlixBus/RegioJet coach to Karlovy Vary Terminal (~1h 25m-1h 30m, hourly)

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants, rounded up or added to the bill

food.name: Becherovka
food.desc: Karlovy Vary's amber herbal liqueur, made here since 1807 from a secret blend of spices; drunk chilled as the thirteenth spring.

places.name: U Svejka

food.name: Spa spring water
food.desc: Hot mineral water sipped through the spout of a porcelain lazensky pohar cup; twelve springs, each a different temperature and mineral load.

places.name: Vridelni Colonnade
places.area: Spa centre, by the Tepla river
places.note: Home of the Vridlo geyser, which shoots water 12 metres up; the hottest and most famous spring.

places.name: Mlynska Colonnade
places.note: Neo-Renaissance colonnade with five springs to try in a row; cups sold at the shops alongside.

places.name: Trzni Colonnade

landmarks: Mill Colonnade (Mlýnská kolonáda)
A stately neo-Renaissance colonnade of 124 columns sheltering five hot mineral springs, this 19th-century masterpiece is the spa town's defining promenade and photo stop.
Hot Spring Colonnade (Vřídelní kolonáda) and Vřídlo Geyser
Inside this modern glass hall, the famous Vřídlo spring erupts up to 12 metres high, spouting 73-degree thermal water at the heart of the spa.
Diana Observation Tower
Reached by a nostalgic funicular through forested hills, this 1914 lookout tower rewards visitors with sweeping panoramas over Karlovy Vary's pastel-painted valley.
Church of St. Mary Magdalene
Kilian Ignaz Dientzenhofer's twin-towered Baroque gem of 1737 rises above the Hot Spring, its ornate dome and crypt among Bohemia's finest sacred architecture.
Grandhotel Pupp
A legendary 18th-century grand hotel that hosted Goethe, Casanova and film stars, its opulent facade famously appeared in Casino Royale and anchors the spa promenade.
Market Colonnade (Tržní kolonáda)
This lacy white Swiss-style wooden colonnade of 1883 shelters the Charles IV Spring, where legend says the emperor discovered the town's healing waters.
Park Colonnade (Sadová kolonáda)
An elegant cast-iron colonnade from 1881 curving through Dvořák Park, its delicate filigree arches frame the Snake Spring and riverside flowerbeds beautifully.
Church of Saints Peter and Paul
Golden onion domes crown this lavish Russian Orthodox church of 1898, built for aristocratic spa guests and gleaming above the villa-lined Westend district.
Jan Becher Museum
Housed in the original factory, this museum reveals the secret history of Becherovka, the herbal liqueur dubbed the town's thirteenth healing spring, with tastings included.
Moser Glassworks and Museum
Watch master glassblowers shape the crystal that has graced royal tables since 1857, then browse the museum's dazzling collection of Moser luxury glassware.

train.note: No direct international trains, though the German border is close - for Nuremberg or Leipzig you change at Cheb or Chomutov. Trains from Prague take about 3h15 and are slower than the coach; the line to Cheb and the Bavarian border is scenic but leisurely. Karlovy Vary has two stations, Horní and Dolní - check which your service uses.

bus.note: The coach is the way to reach Karlovy Vary. RegioJet (https://www.regiojet.com/) and FlixBus run from Prague's Florenc terminal in about 2h15, considerably faster than the train, with frequent departures. The bus terminal is next to Dolní nádraží. Carry your passport or EU ID card for onward German services.

ferry.note: Czechia is landlocked and the Teplá river through the spa colonnade is a stream rather than a waterway, so there are no ferries.

half.name: Loket Castle
half.blurb: A medieval castle sits on a granite outcrop encircled by a bend in the Ohře River, in a small walled town.

half.name: Mariánské Lázně
half.blurb: A second spa town with singing fountains and colonnaded promenades draws on mineral springs similar to those in Karlovy Vary.

half.name: Cheb
half.blurb: A Romanesque imperial castle and a medieval square lined with leaning half-timbered houses mark this town near the German border.

half.name: Bečov nad Teplou
half.blurb: A hilltop castle holds the Bečov reliquary, a jewel-encrusted 12th-century gold container rediscovered hidden in a swamp after World War II.
